questions.stem: How can you test a leaf for starch to show photosynthesis has occurred?

options.text: Boil the leaf in water, then in ethanol, rinse, and add iodine solution
Place the leaf in Biuret reagent
Weigh the leaf before and after

questions.explanation: The starch test involves boiling the leaf to kill cells, placing it in hot ethanol to remove chlorophyll, rinsing in water, then adding iodine solution. A blue-black colour indicates starch is present.

questions.stem: Why is the leaf boiled in ethanol during the starch test?

options.text: To add starch to the leaf
To remove the green chlorophyll so colour changes can be seen clearly

questions.explanation: Ethanol dissolves chlorophyll, removing the green colour from the leaf. This is necessary so that the colour change with iodine solution can be clearly observed.

questions.stem: In an experiment to show light is needed for photosynthesis, part of a leaf is covered with foil. What result would you expect?

options.text: The whole leaf turns blue-black with iodine
Only the uncovered part turns blue-black with iodine
Only the covered part turns blue-black

questions.explanation: Only the uncovered part of the leaf, which received light, can photosynthesise and produce starch. The covered part has no starch and remains yellow-brown with iodine.

questions.stem: How can you show that carbon dioxide is needed for photosynthesis?

options.text: Place the plant in a sealed container with sodium hydroxide to absorb CO2

questions.explanation: Sodium hydroxide absorbs carbon dioxide from the air around the plant. Without CO2, the leaf cannot photosynthesise and will test negative for starch.

questions.stem: Pondweed can be used to measure the rate of photosynthesis by counting:

options.text: The colour change of the water
The number of oxygen bubbles released per minute

questions.explanation: Aquatic pondweed (such as Elodea) releases oxygen bubbles during photosynthesis. Counting bubbles per minute gives a measure of the rate of photosynthesis.

questions.stem: Why should the leaf be destarched before a photosynthesis experiment?

options.text: To ensure any starch found is produced only during the experiment, not before
To increase the rate of photosynthesis

questions.explanation: Destarching (keeping the plant in darkness for 48 hours) removes existing starch from leaves, so any starch detected after the experiment must have been produced during the experiment.

questions.stem: A variegated leaf has green and white areas. After testing for starch, which areas turn blue-black?
questions.explanation: Only the green areas contain chlorophyll and can photosynthesise. The green areas produce starch and turn blue-black with iodine, while the white areas (lacking chlorophyll) do not.
